s: On what basis are linguistic minorities in India identified?
o: by notification under the NCM Act
by the National Commission for Minorities
x: Linguistic minorities are identified State-wise and handled by the Special Officer under Article 350B; religious minorities are dealt with by the NCM.

s: In which year was the office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities established?
x: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957.

s: Article 29(2) bars denial of admission to State-aided institutions on grounds only of religion, race, caste or ____.
x: Article 29(2) lists religion, race, caste and language; sex and place of birth are not in this list.

s: Which provision bars denial of admission to State-maintained or State-aided educational institutions on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language?
x: Article 29(2) bars such denial; Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any distinct section of citizens.

s: A State seeks to deny aid to an educational institution solely because it is managed by a linguistic minority. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
x: Article 30(2) provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.

s: Clause (1A) of Article 30, which protects the right of minorities to establish educational institutions when their property is compulsorily acquired, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The 44th Amendment, which removed the right to property, added Article 30(1A) so that removal of that right does not affect minorities' right to establish institutions and compensation is ensured on acquisition. The 7th Amendment (1956) inserted Articles 350A and 350B; the 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5) after P.A. Inamdar; the 42nd Amendment did not add Article 30(1A).

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 350A and 350B?
x: The 7th Amendment, 1956, linked to States reorganisation, inserted Articles 350A and 350B.

s: Who appoints the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B?
x: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer is appointed by the President and reports to the President.

s: Which Article provides for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage?
x: Article 350A provides for mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage; Article 350B provides for the Special Officer.

s: Which Article bars the State from discriminating against minority educational institutions in granting aid?
x: Under Article 30 the State cannot discriminate against minority institutions in aid; it may regulate standards without destroying minority character.

s: Which Article of the Constitution gives any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture the right to conserve it?
x: Article 29(1) protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture; it is not limited to minorities, unlike Article 30.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities?
x: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities has its headquarters in New Delhi: set up there in 1957, moved to Allahabad (Prayagraj) for a time, and back in New Delhi since 2015. (Earlier app key: Prayagraj.)

s: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the President to recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of a State's population?
x: Article 347 lets the President recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of a State's population.

s: Which Article of the Constitution allows every person to submit a representation for redress of a grievance in any language used in the Union or in the State?
x: Article 350 allows representations for redress of grievances in any language used in the Union or the State.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)
A. Article 347
B. Article 350
C. Article 350A
D. Article 350B
List-II (Provision)
1. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
2. Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
3. Representation for grievances in any language
4. Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Art. 347 = recognition of a language of a State's population; Art. 350 = grievances in any language; Art. 350A = mother-tongue instruction; Art. 350B = Special Officer.

s: For the purposes of the National Commission for Minorities Act, a community is a minority when it is:
o: Defined as such in the Act
x: Under Section 2(c) of the NCM Act, a minority is any community notified by the Central Government. States may also name their own minorities for State purposes.

s: After T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002), with reference to the population position in which unit is minority status decided?
x: The State, not the whole of India, is the unit for deciding minority status; minority rights are not absolute and may be regulated.

s: Which one of the following communities is NOT among the notified minority communities?
x: The notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. Jews are not included in this listed group.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding State designation of minorities is correct?
o: Jains were declared a minority simultaneously by all States in 2014.
Only the Union Government can designate a community as a minority.
States can designate their own minorities, and 11 States had declared Jains a minority before 2014.
States cannot designate minorities unless authorised by the Supreme Court.
x: States have the power to designate their own minorities. Before 2014, 11 States had declared Jains a minority.

s: In which year were Jains notified as a minority community?
x: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993; Jains were added in 2014.

s: The Constitution refers to the term ‘minority’ in which of the following Articles, without defining it?
x: The Constitution uses the term ‘minority’ in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B, but does not provide a general definition of the term.

s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised because it gives the Centre:
o: exclusive power to appoint State minority commissions
power to amend the Constitution without Parliament
x: Section 2(c) has been criticised as giving the Centre ‘unbridled power’ to notify minorities, raising concerns in the context of T.M.A. Pai.

s: Which is the largest notified minority community in India as per Census 2011?
x: Muslims form 14.2% of the population (Census 2011), the largest minority; Christians are 2.3% and Sikhs 1.7%.

s: The six notified minority communities together make up about what share of India's population?
x: The six notified minorities are about 19% of the population; 14.2% is the share of Muslims alone.

s:
Consider the following statements about notified minority communities:
1. Five communities were notified in 1993.
2. Jews are a notified minority community.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993 and Jains in 2014; Jews are not notified.

s: Which of the following statements about minority rights in India is correct?
o: Minority rights are absolute and cannot be regulated
Minority status is decided on an all-India basis
The State may regulate standards in minority institutions but cannot take away their management
Only religious minorities can set up educational institutions
x: Minority rights are not absolute: the State may regulate standards but cannot take away management; status is decided State-wise.

s: Which is the second largest religious minority in India as per Census 2011?
x: Census 2011: Muslims 14.2% are the largest minority, followed by Christians 2.3% and Sikhs 1.7%.

s: Under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, a 'minority' means a community notified as such by the Central Government under which provision?
x: Under Section 2(c) of the NCM Act, 1992, a minority means any community notified by the Central Government. Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any section of citizens, and Section 9 of the Waqf Act, 1995 concerns the Central Waqf Council.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Conducting elections to minority educational institutions
Looking into specific complaints relating to deprivation of minority safeguards
Monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards for minorities
x: The Commission evaluates development, monitors safeguards, examines complaints and recommends measures; conducting elections to minority educational institutions is not one of its stated functions.

s: While inquiring into complaints, the National Commission for Minorities has the powers of which of the following?
x: The NCM has civil-court-like powers such as summoning witnesses and calling for records; it cannot impose criminal sentences.

s: In which year did the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993 lapse?
x: The Act lapsed in 2004; the NCSK continues as a non-statutory body with tenure extended by resolution.

s: How many members of the National Commission for Minorities, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities?
x: The NCM has seven members; five, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities, so all seven need not be.

s: Who was the first chairman of the statutory National Commission for Minorities?
x: The first statutory NCM (1993) was chaired by Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan; Harjit Singh Grewal is Chairperson in 2026.

s: In which year was the post of Vice-Chairperson, which made the NCM a seven-member body, added?
x: A 1995 amendment added the Vice-Chairperson, giving Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + 5 Members = 7.

s: Which ministry's resolution set up the non-statutory Minorities Commission of 1978?
x: The 1978 Minorities Commission came by an MHA resolution; the Ministry of Minority Affairs came only in 2006.

s: In which year was the Ministry of Minority Affairs created?
x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was set up in 2006; Haj was added to it in October 2016.

s: Statutory State Minorities Commissions exist in how many States/UTs?
x: State Minorities Commissions are statutory in 19 States/UTs, including Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

s: What is the tenure of members of the National Commission for Minorities?
x: NCM members hold office for 3 years.

s: In which year was the National Commission for Minorities Act, which made the Minorities Commission a statutory body, enacted?
x: The non-statutory Minorities Commission came in 1978; the NCM Act was enacted in 1992 and the first statutory Commission was constituted in 1993.

s: Who nominates the Chairperson and Members of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
x: The NCM's Chairperson and Members are nominated by the Central Government, not the President.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Minorities:
1. It is a constitutional body.
2. It has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The NCM is a statutory body under the NCM Act, 1992, not a constitutional body; it has seven members including the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson.

s: Who was the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026?
x: In July 2026 Harjit Singh Grewal was NCM Chairperson and Munawari Begum Vice-Chairperson; only 4 of 7 posts were filled.

s: In which year was Haj management added to the work of the Ministry of Minority Affairs?
x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was created in 2006, and Haj was added to it in October 2016.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 29 – Protection of a section's distinct language, script or culture
Article 30 – Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
Ranganath Misra Commission – First Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities
Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan – First Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities
x: Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan was the first NCM chairman; the Ranganath Misra Commission studied religious and linguistic minorities.

s: How many judges decided T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002)?
x: An 11-judge Bench made the State the unit for minority status and allowed regulation, not control, of minority institutions.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: P.A. Inamdar (2005) — Presidential reference under Article 143
In re Kerala Education Bill (1957) — 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status
St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) — right to administer protected, subject to standards and excellence regulations
T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) — seven-judge Bench and no State quota in unaided institutions
x: C is correct: St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) protected the right to administer, allowing regulation only for standards and excellence. The others are mismatched: the Article 143 Presidential reference was the Kerala Education Bill case, not P.A. Inamdar; the 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status belong to T.M.A. Pai; the seven-judge Bench barring State quotas in unaided institutions was P.A. Inamdar.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the decision in P.A. Inamdar (2005)?
o: A seven-judge Bench held that the State could impose its quota in unaided institutions without limitation.
A seven-judge Bench held that there could be no State quota or reservation in unaided institutions, contributing to the subsequent 93rd Amendment framework.
An 11-judge Bench abolished the distinction between aided and unaided institutions.
The Court held that minority status must be determined at the national level.
x: P.A. Inamdar was decided by a seven-judge Bench and held that the State could not impose its quota or reservation in unaided institutions. The decision was followed by the constitutional development associated with Article 15(5) through the 93rd Amendment.

s: The decision in Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) is associated with which of the following?
o: Directing the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority
Imposing reservation quotas on unaided minority institutions
Declaring that minority status must be determined nationally
Declining to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority and leaving the matter to the States
x: The Court declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority, leaving the matter to the States and cautioning against the multiplication of minority claims.

s: In what form did In re Kerala Education Bill (1958) come before the Supreme Court?
o: appeal from the Kerala High Court
x: The Kerala Education Bill case was an Article 143 Presidential reference; it held Article 30 is not absolute.

s: Which case held that minority institutions may be regulated only for standards and excellence?
o: Bal Patil v. Union of India
P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra
St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
x: St. Xavier's College (1974) protected the right to administer and allowed regulation only for standards and excellence.

s: How many judges decided P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra (2005)?
x: P.A. Inamdar was a 7-judge Bench; the 11-judge Bench was T.M.A. Pai (2002).

s: In St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi (1992), up to what share of seats could an aided minority college prefer its own community?
x: St. Stephen's held that an aided minority college may prefer its own community up to about 50% of seats.

s: Which case held that the State cannot impose reservation on unaided professional institutions?
o: P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra
T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
x: P.A. Inamdar (2005) barred reservation in unaided institutions; T.M.A. Pai made the State the unit for minority status.

s: Which body determines the minority status of an educational institution and issues minority institution certificates?
o: National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions
x: The NCMEI determines minority status, decides affiliation disputes and issues minority certificates, with civil court powers.

s: In which year was the Act establishing the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions passed?
x: The NCMEI is associated with the 2004 Act; statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/UTs, including Andhra Pradesh.

s: In which year was the first National Foundation for Communal Harmony established?
x: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was set up in 1992. 1983 is the 15-Point Programme and 2005 the Sachar Committee.

s: When did the Sachar Committee, set up in 2005 and chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar, submit its report?
x: The Sachar Committee was set up by the Prime Minister in 2005 and submitted its report in November 2006.

s: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in which areas?
x: The Sachar Committee found Muslims badly under-represented in public jobs and higher education, against their share of the population.

s: In which year was the Sachar Committee, a Prime Minister's High-Level Committee, set up?
x: The Sachar Committee was set up in March 2005 and reported in November 2006.

s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal associated with the Sachar Committee?
x: The Sachar Committee proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, National Data Bank and Assessment and Monitoring Authority. A National Linguistic Minorities Commission was not listed among its proposals.

s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was associated with which of the following recommendations?
o: Replacement of all State languages by Hindi
A 15% reservation and delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion
Creation of the National Data Bank for census purposes only
x: The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities, chaired by Justice Ranganath Misra, suggested a 15% quota for minorities and delinking SC status from religion.

s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was established in which year?
x: The Ranganath Misra Commission on religious and linguistic minorities was set up in 2004. The Sachar Committee followed in 2005.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities – Amitabh Kundu
x: The Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee was chaired by Amitabh Kundu; the Sachar Committee by Rajinder Sachar and the minorities commission by Justice Ranganath Misra.

s: In which year did the Gopal Singh Committee on minorities submit its report?
x: The Gopal Singh panel on minorities reported in 1983; the Ranganath Misra Commission came in 2004 and Sachar in 2005.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ashraf — upper or claimed foreign origin
Ajlaf — the most deprived Dalit Muslim group
x: Arzal, rather than Ajlaf, was described as the Dalit Muslim group and the most deprived category. Ajlaf was identified as a backward group requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.

s: Whose socio-economic and educational status did the Sachar Committee study?
x: The Sachar Committee (2005-06) studied the socio-economic and educational status of Muslims.

s: In which year did the Ranganath Misra Commission submit its report?
x: The Ranganath Misra Commission was constituted in 2004 and reported in 2007.

s: The Ranganath Misra Commission recommended what reservation for Muslims?
x: It recommended 15% reservation for minorities, of which 10% for Muslims.

s: Who chaired the Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee (2013-14)?
x: The Kundu Committee under Prof. Amitabh Kundu evaluated the post-Sachar position and found gaps persisting.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to Muslim groups described by the Sachar Committee?
o: Arzal – claimed foreign or upper-caste origin
Ajlaf – need attention like Hindu OBCs
x: Ajlaf (commoners, lower-caste converts) need attention like Hindu OBCs; Arzal are Dalit Muslims and Ashraf the upper group.

s: Which committee recommended a Diversity Index, an anti-discrimination law and an Equal Opportunity Commission after evaluating the follow-up of Sachar?
x: The Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee under Prof. Amitabh Kundu (2013-14) found gaps persisting and recommended these measures.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Communal Award came in 1932. The National Integration Council began in 1961 and the National Foundation for Communal Harmony in 1992.

s: In which year was the National Integration Council set up under Jawaharlal Nehru?
x: The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 under Nehru; the National Foundation for Communal Harmony came in 1992.

s: Urdu was made the second official language of Andhra Pradesh under which law?
x: Urdu is AP's second official language under the AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 bifurcated the State; the Official Languages Act, 1963 deals with the Union's official languages; the 7th Amendment, 1956 inserted Articles 350A and 350B.

s: Andhra Pradesh's G.O. 1065 (August 2026) provides what BC reservation in urban local body polls?
x: G.O. 1065 gives 33.33% BC reservation in ULB polls; AP's 138 BC communities are in Groups A-E.

s: What monthly honorarium does Andhra Pradesh pay imams?
x: AP pays Rs 10,000 a month to imams and Rs 5,000 to muezzins.

s: How much marriage aid does Andhra Pradesh's Shaadi Tohfa (2020) give to minority brides?
x: Shaadi Tohfa (October 2020) gives Rs 1 lakh; the earlier Dulhan scheme gave Rs 50,000.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, Backward Classes comprise how many communities in Groups A-E?
x: AP's BCs (43.17% of the population) comprise 138 communities in Groups A-E.

s:
Consider the following statements about minority welfare in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a statutory State Minorities Commission.
2. The Dulhan scheme gives Rs 1 lakh to minority brides.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP has a statutory State Minorities Commission; Dulhan gives Rs 50,000, while Rs 1 lakh is under Shaadi Tohfa.

s: Backward Classes form about what share of Andhra Pradesh's population?
x: BCs are about 43.17% of AP's population, in 138 communities under Groups A-E.

s: What monthly honorarium does Andhra Pradesh pay muezzins?
x: Andhra Pradesh pays Rs 10,000 a month to imams and Rs 5,000 a month to muezzins.

s: What happened to the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, which affected the Denotified Tribes?
x: Denotified Tribes had been branded under the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, which was repealed in 1952.

s: Who administers the SEED Scheme Portal for applications from Denotified Tribe communities?
x: The SEED portal, which takes DNT applications for health insurance, coaching and housing, is run by the Department of Social Justice, not the NTA.

s: What percentage of PM-YASASVI slots is earmarked for girls?
x: PM-YASASVI reserves 30 percent of slots for girls and follows a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio.

s: Under which ministry does the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) function?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: NBCFDC (1992) is under MoSJE; NMDFC is under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, and both lend through State Channelising Agencies.

s: For whom is the NBCFDC's New Swarnima scheme meant?
x: New Swarnima is for women and Saksham for young professionals; Virasat loans for artisans are associated with NMDFC.

s: How is the credit support structured under PM Vishwakarma?
o: Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 5 lakh without any interest
Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 2 lakh at 5 percent interest
Rs 15,000 followed by Rs 2 lakh at 12 percent interest
Rs 2 lakh followed by Rs 1 lakh at 10 percent interest
x: The scheme provides collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh initially and an additional Rs 2 lakh, with the credit carrying a 5 percent interest rate.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for PM Vishwakarma?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: MSME is the nodal ministry; MSDE and the Department of Financial Services are also involved in implementation.

s: The Idate Commission found about how many Denotified Tribes that had never been classified?
x: About 267-268 DNTs had never been classified, while about 1,200 were already in SC, ST or OBC lists.

s: In which year was the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) established?
x: NSFDC came in 1989 for SCs, NBCFDC in 1992 for Backward Classes and NSTFDC in 2001 for STs; NMDFC serves minorities.

s: What was the main reason cited for the low expenditure under the SEED scheme?
o: States did not issue DNT certificates
the scheme covered only urban areas
the Union Government withdrew the scheme
beneficiaries were excluded from health insurance
x: Low expenditure was attributed to the failure of States to issue certificates for Denotified Tribes.

s: Which commission was the first to examine the condition of Denotified Tribes among the commissions mentioned below?
x: The Renke Commission, whose report was submitted in 2008, was the first such commission mentioned for Denotified Tribes.

s: Whom does PM Vishwakarma mainly target?
x: PM Vishwakarma is intended for artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades. It is not a fishermen's scheme.

s: What is the stated outlay of the SEED scheme, launched in 2022?
x: SEED (2022) has an outlay of Rs 200 crore and covers coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing for incomes below Rs 2.5 lakh.

s: The PM-YASASVI Portal is meant for scholarship application and disbursement for which groups?
o: OBC, EBC and nomadic tribe students
x: The PM-YASASVI portal handles scholarship applications and payments for OBC, EBC and denotified/nomadic tribe students.

s: In which year was PM Vishwakarma launched on Vishwakarma Jayanti?
x: The scheme was launched on 17 September 2023, Vishwakarma Jayanti.

s: Which scheme funds SC students in higher education at IITs and IIMs?
x: SHREYAS supports higher education and funds 8,571 SC students at IITs and IIMs.

s: PM-YASASVI is for OBC, EBC and DNT students with family income below what limit?
x: PM-YASASVI (2021) covers OBC/EBC/DNT students with income below Rs 2.5 lakh, with 30% slots for girls.

s: Through which agencies do NBCFDC and NMDFC lend to beneficiaries?
x: Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through State Channelising Agencies.

s: For whom are NMDFC's Virasat loans meant?
x: Virasat gives loans to minority artisans; New Swarnima (women) and Saksham (young professionals) are NBCFDC schemes.

s: PM Vishwakarma covers artisans in how many trades?
x: PM Vishwakarma, launched on 17 September 2023, covers artisans in 18 trades.

s: For whom is the NBCFDC's Saksham scheme meant?
x: NBCFDC's Saksham is for young professionals; New Swarnima is for women.

s: Under which ministry does the National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC) function?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: NMDFC is a Section 8 company under the Ministry of Minority Affairs; it lends through State Channelising Agencies.

s: In which year was the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) set up?
x: NSTFDC was set up in 2001; NSFDC dates from 1989 and NBCFDC from 1992.

s: In which Census are Denotified Tribes (DNTs) to be counted?
x: Census 2027 will count Denotified Tribes.

s: In which year was the PM's New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities introduced?
x: The programme, introduced in 2006, covers education, jobs, living conditions, prevention of communal violence and earmarked outlays.

s: Under the PM's New 15 Point Programme, about what share of targets and outlays in selected schemes is earmarked for minorities?
x: The programme earmarks about 15 percent of targets and outlays in selected schemes, aims to prevent communal riots and is monitored by review committees.

s: In which year was the original 15-Point Programme for minorities introduced?
x: The original 15-Point Programme dates from 1983; the PM's New 15 Point Programme came in 2006.

s: Which of the following is NOT an aim of the PM's New 15 Point Programme?
o: Fair share in jobs and economic activity
x: The four aims are education, jobs and economic activity, living conditions and prevention of riots; delinking SC status from religion was a Ranganath Misra recommendation.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Hamari Dharohar — preserving the heritage of minorities
Seekho aur Kamao — skill upgradation and placement
Nai Manzil — education and skilling for school dropouts
Nai Roshni — free coaching after clearing civil services preliminaries
x: Nai Roshni concerns leadership training for minority women. Free coaching and post-preliminary support are associated with Naya Savera and Nai Udaan.

s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five schemes merged into PM VIKAS?
x: PM VIKAS merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil. PMJVK is not one of the five merged schemes.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes PMJVK?
o: It is a Central Sector Scheme limited to minority students pursuing higher education.
It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for area development in minority concentration areas.
It is a constitutional programme implemented by the Election Commission.
It is a State scheme restricted to urban minority households.
x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at area development in minority concentration areas.

s: Which minority scheme brings together skill development, artisan support and entrepreneurship?
x: PM-VIKAS converges skill training, support for artisans and entrepreneurship for minorities.

s: Which of the following statements about Naya Savera & Nai Udaan is incorrect?
o: It is meant for students clearing UPSC and SSC Main examinations.
It provides financial support to minority students.
It provides free coaching to minority students.
It is associated with the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
x: Option A is incorrect: Naya Savera and Nai Udaan support minority students who clear the UPSC or SSC prelims, not the mains.

s: What is the full form of PM VIKAS, a Central Sector scheme of 2022 merging five minority schemes?
o: Pradhan Mantri Vikas Aur Kaushal Samvardhan
Pradhan Mantri Virasat Aur Kala Sanrakshan
x: PM VIKAS means Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan; it merges five schemes and runs until 2025-26.

s: PM Jan Vikas Karyakram was restructured from which earlier programme?
x: PMJVK was restructured from the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP), which dates from 2008-09.

s: What is the focus of the Nai Roshni (2013) scheme?
o: Education and skills for school dropouts
x: Nai Roshni is leadership training for minority women; Nai Manzil serves dropouts and Nai Udaan supports those who clear prelims.

s: Which minority scheme combines education and skills for school dropouts?
x: Nai Manzil (2015) gives education plus skills to school dropouts.

s: What types of scheme are PM VIKAS and PM Jan Vikas Karyakram, respectively?
x: PM VIKAS is a Central Sector scheme, while PMJVK is Centrally Sponsored.

s: What share of PM VIKAS skilling seats is reserved for women?
x: PM VIKAS reserves 33% of skilling seats for women; 30% is the PM-YASASVI share for girls.

s: Up to what family income are post-matric scholarships given to minority students?
x: The minority post-matric scholarship has an income ceiling of Rs 2 lakh, paid by DBT through the National Scholarship Portal.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Seekho aur Kamao – modern skilling with placement
x: Nai Roshni is leadership training for minority women; the scheme for school dropouts is Nai Manzil.

s: The Wakf (Amendment) Act, 2013 enabled which body to direct State Waqf Boards?
x: The 2013 amendment let the Central Waqf Council direct State Boards and barred sale, gift, mortgage, exchange and transfer of waqf property.

s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Waqf Act, 1954
B. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2013
C. Waqf Act, 1995
D. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025
x: The correct sequence is Waqf Act 1954, Waqf Act 1995, Waqf (Amendment) Act 2013, and Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025.

s: Which of the following statements about the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 is correct?
o: Only Muslim members could thereafter serve on the Central Waqf Council and State Boards.
Waqf by user was abolished even for all properties registered before the amendment.
Waqf by user survived only for properties registered before the law.
The Act prohibited the use of any central portal for waqf properties.
x: Under the 2025 Act, waqf by user survived only for properties registered before the law. The Act also provided for non-Muslim members and a central portal.

s: Under the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, within what period were all waqf properties to be placed on a central portal?
x: The 2025 amendment required waqf properties on a central portal within six months; the UMEED portal was launched in June 2025.

s: Which of the following describes the Central Waqf Council?
o: A temporary executive committee established in 1995 to conduct elections
A statutory body established in 1964 to advise the Centre on State Waqf Boards
A judicial body established in 2025 to decide all land disputes
A constitutional body established in 1950 to supervise courts
x: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body established in 1964. Its principal role is to advise the Central Government on State Waqf Boards.

s:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court's interim order of September 2025 stayed the five-years-practising-Islam condition in the Waqf (Amendment) Act.
Reason (R): The same order accepted the change applying the Limitation Act.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: The order stayed the five-year condition and the Collector's power and accepted the Limitation Act change; the two holdings are separate, so R does not explain A.

s: The Waqf Act, 1995 primarily deals with which of the following?
x: The Waqf Act, 1995, governs the administration of waqf properties. Tribal forest rights fall under the Forest Rights Act, and free legal aid under the Legal Services Authorities Act.

s: What new name did the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 give to the Waqf Act, 1995?
x: With the 2025 Act (assent 5 April 2025), the 1995 Act was renamed the UMEED Act.

s: At what number did the Supreme Court's interim order of September 2025 cap non-Muslim members of a State Waqf Board?
x: The order capped non-Muslims at 3 on a State Board and 4 on the Central Waqf Council.

s: Under the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, within how many days does an appeal lie to the High Court?
x: The 2025 Act provides an appeal to the High Court within 90 days and applies the Limitation Act.

s: On which date was the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 introduced in the Lok Sabha?
x: The Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 8 August 2024; the Act got assent on 5 April 2025.

s: What is the name of the central portal launched in June 2025 for waqf properties?
x: Under the 2025 Act all waqf properties go on a central portal, the UMEED portal (June 2025).

s: Under the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, at least how many non-Muslim members must each State Waqf Board have?
x: The 2025 Act requires at least two non-Muslim members per Board; the SC's interim order capped them at three for a State Board.

s: How much hospitalisation cover did the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY), launched in 2008 for BPL families, provide?
x: RSBY (2008) gave BPL families ₹30,000 hospitalisation cover and was later subsumed in AB-PMJAY.

s: Which scheme replaced the Swavalamban scheme for unorganised workers joining NPS-Lite in 2015?
x: Swavalamban (2010) was replaced by the Atal Pension Yojana in 2015; Ashraya Bima Yojana (2001, LIC) was for workers who lost jobs.

s: Which body administers the Atal Pension Yojana (2015)?
x: APY gives a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000–₹5,000 from age 60 and is run by PFRDA.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMJJBY — accident death and disability cover
PMSBY — ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause
PMJJBY — ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause
Atal Pension Yojana — ₹436 annual premium for life cover
x: PMJJBY provides ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause for an annual premium of ₹436. PMSBY concerns accidental death and disability cover.

s: Which of the following statements about ESIC coverage is correct?
o: It is restricted to establishments in selected States only.
It is compulsory only for units employing fewer than 10 persons.
It is pan-India and voluntary for units employing fewer than 10 persons.
It applies exclusively to government establishments.
x: ESIC coverage is pan-India and voluntary for establishments with fewer than 10 employees.

s: What is the entry age for PMJJBY?
x: PMJJBY is the only one with 18-50; PM-SYM, NPS-Traders and APY are 18-40 and PMSBY 18-70.

s: Which scheme gives accidental death and disability cover of Rs 2 lakh for Rs 20 a year?
x: PMSBY is an accident scheme (Rs 20/year); PMJJBY is life cover for death from any cause (Rs 436/year).

s: What is the wage ceiling for ESIC coverage?
x: The ESI wage ceiling is Rs 21,000 a month (since 2017).

s: To what amount was the EPFO wage ceiling raised from Rs 15,000 in September 2026?
x: The EPFO wage ceiling rose from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 in September 2026.

s: Up to what annual turnover is NPS-Traders open to traders?
x: NPS-Traders (September 2019) covers traders aged 18-40 with turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore.

s: For whom was the Ashraya Bima Yojana (2001) meant?
x: Ashraya Bima Yojana (2001, LIC) covered workers who lost their jobs; RSBY was for BPL families.

s:
Consider the following statements about PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM):
1. Its entry age is 18-40 years.
2. Members of NPS are also eligible for it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: PM-SYM is for 18-40 year olds; EPFO, ESIC and government-funded NPS members are excluded.

s: What is the entry age for PM-SYM, which assures ₹3,000 a month from age 60?
x: PM-SYM entry age is 18-40 (18-50 is PMJJBY); it covers unorganised workers earning up to ₹15,000 a month.

s: What is the entry age for joining the Atal Pension Yojana?
x: The Atal Pension Yojana is open to people aged 18-40; only PMJJBY has an 18-50 entry age.

s: What monthly pension does the Atal Pension Yojana guarantee from the age of 60?
x: APY, run by PFRDA, gives a pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 a month from age 60 depending on contribution.

s: Up to what monthly income can unorganised workers join the PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) scheme?
x: PM-SYM is for unorganised workers aged 18-40 earning up to Rs 15,000 a month.

s: In which scheme was the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) later subsumed?
x: RSBY (2008), which gave BPL families Rs 30,000 hospitalisation cover, was later subsumed in AB-PMJAY.

s: In which year was the Swavalamban scheme for unorganised workers in NPS-Lite launched?
x: Swavalamban began in 2010 with a government co-contribution and was replaced by APY in 2015.

s: What is the entry age for the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?
x: PMSBY, the accident cover scheme, is open to those aged 18-70.

s: What is the annual premium of the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?
x: PMJJBY gives Rs 2 lakh life cover for a premium of Rs 436 a year.

s: What do first-time employees get under the PMVBRY?
o: One month's wage, up to Rs 15,000
A pension of Rs 3,000 a month
x: PMVBRY (Rs 99,446 crore for 3.5 crore jobs) gives first-time employees one month's wage, up to Rs 15,000.

s: In which year was the Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana launched?
x: The Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana was launched on 2 October 2007.

s: For whom was the Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (2007) meant?
x: AABY gave insurance cover to the head or one earning member of rural landless households, through LIC.

s: Which of the following is NOT a condition that excludes a person from PM-SYM and NPS-Traders eligibility?
o: Being a worker in the unorganised sector
x: Membership of EPFO, ESIC or government-funded NPS, and being an income-tax payer, excludes eligibility. Being an unorganised-sector worker is not an exclusion; PM-SYM is specifically intended for such workers.

s: At the district level, which body is responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976?
x: District-level Vigilance Committees are responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the 1976 Act.

s: Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits begar and other forms of forced labour, is given effect for bonded labour mainly through which law?
x: Article 23 bans begar and forced labour, and the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 abolishes bonded labour, with district Vigilance Committees to identify and release bonded labourers. The Contract Labour Act regulates contract labour, the Minimum Wages Act fixes wages, and the 2008 Act set up the National Social Security Board for unorganised workers.

s: In which year was the Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer launched?
x: The rehabilitation scheme dates from 2016 (revised 2021); the Abolition Act is of 1976.

s: To what amount did the 2021 revision of the bonded labour rehabilitation scheme raise immediate aid?
x: The 2021 revision raised immediate aid to Rs 30,000; the scheme is 100% centrally funded.

s: How is the Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer (2016) funded?
x: The 2016 scheme is 100% centrally funded and gives Rs 1, 2 or 3 lakh by category.

s: Who appoints Inspectors under the Factories Act, 1948?
x: Inspectors are appointed by the State Government, and every District Magistrate is an Inspector for his district.

s: Under the Factories Act 1948, if no manager is named, who is deemed to be the manager?
x: If no manager is named, the occupier is deemed the manager.

s: What minimum age for factory work did the Factories Act, 1948 fix, the first post-1947 law to do so?
x: The Factories Act fixed 14 years as the minimum age for factory work.

s: Under the Factories Act, 1948, who is an Inspector for his district by virtue of his office?
x: Inspectors are appointed by the State Government, and every District Magistrate is an Inspector for his district.

s: On which date did the four Labour Codes come into force in India?
x: The Code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Social Security Code and OSH Code came into force on 21 November 2025.

s: How many central labour laws were consolidated into the four Labour Codes?
x: The four Labour Codes consolidate 29 central labour laws.

s: How many central labour laws, including the Factories Act, 1948, are subsumed by the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020?
x: The OSH Code, 2020 replaces 13 laws on safety, health and working conditions, including the Factories Act, 1948.

s: Which of the following laws is NOT subsumed by the Code on Wages, 2019?
x: The Code on Wages amalgamates the Payment of Wages, Minimum Wages, Payment of Bonus and Equal Remuneration Acts; the Industrial Disputes Act is not one of them.

s: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, the Inspector is renamed as what?
x: Section 51 of the Code on Wages replaces the Inspector with an Inspector-cum-Facilitator, who both enforces and guides.

s: The four Labour Codes together replaced how many central labour laws?
x: The four Codes replaced 29 central labour laws.

s: Which of the four Labour Codes was enacted in 2019?
x: The Code on Wages came in 2019; the other three Codes are of 2020.

s: On which date did all four Labour Codes come into force?
x: All four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025.

s: Into which Code has the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 been subsumed?
x: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 went into the Industrial Relations Code.

s: In which year was the Indian Labour Conference last held, a point raised in criticism of the Labour Codes?
x: Critics note that the Indian Labour Conference has not been held since 2015.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched under the Industrial Relations Code?
o: Prior permission for layoff, retrenchment and closure – 300 workers
Earlier threshold for layoff permission – 50 workers
x: Prior permission is now needed only for establishments with 300 or more workers (earlier 100); the contract labour threshold rose from 20 to 50.

s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, after how long do fixed-term workers become eligible for gratuity?
x: Fixed-term workers get the same wages and benefits as permanent workers and gratuity after one year.

s: A trade union proposes to commence a strike five days after giving notice. Under the Industrial Relations Code, this proposal is:
o: Not permissible only when the establishment has more than 500 workers
Permissible if the establishment has fewer than 300 workers
Not permissible because a strike cannot occur within 14 days of giving notice
Permissible because notice has been given in writing
x: A strike cannot be held within 14 days of giving notice. The Code also prohibits a strike without notice within the preceding 60 days before striking.

s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, Standing Orders apply to establishments with at least how many workers?
x: The Standing Orders threshold, like the layoff permission threshold, is 300 workers.

s: Under the labour codes, to how many workers has the threshold for applying contract labour provisions been raised from 20?
x: The contract labour threshold has been raised from 20 to 50 workers; 300 is the layoff permission threshold.

s: Into which Code has the Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 been merged?
x: The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 was merged into the Code on Social Security, 2020.

s: Which of the following is listed in Schedule I of the Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008?
x: Schedule I lists schemes such as the National Family Benefit Scheme, Janani Suraksha Yojana and RSBY; Atal Pension Yojana is not in it.

s: Roughly what share of India's about 600 million workers is informal?
x: Over 90% of India's roughly 600 million workers are informal; 77% is the NCEUS figure for people living on under Rs 20 a day.

s: NCEUS found that what share of Indians were living on under Rs 20 a day?
x: The Arjun Sengupta-led NCEUS found 77% living on under Rs 20 a day.

s: Which body did the Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 set up?
o: National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector
x: The 2008 Act set up a National Social Security Board, with welfare schemes listed in Schedule I.

s: Who was the chairman of the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS), set up in 2004?
x: NCEUS was set up in 2004 under Arjun Sengupta; it found 77% of Indians living on under Rs 20 a day.

s: What 12-digit number does the e-Shram portal give every registered unorganised worker?
x: e-Shram, India's first Aadhaar-seeded national database of unorganised workers, gives each worker a 12-digit UAN.

s: Which one of the following persons is eligible for registration on the e-Shram portal?
o: A 15-year-old unorganised worker who is not an income-tax payer
A 25-year-old unorganised worker who is an income-tax payer
A 40-year-old unorganised worker who is not an income-tax payer and is not covered by EPFO or ESIC
A 62-year-old unorganised worker who is not covered by any social-security scheme
x: Eligibility covers unorganised workers aged 16 to 59 who are not income-tax payers and are not members of EPFO or ESIC.

s: When was the e-Shram portal launched?
x: The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched e-Shram on 26 August 2021.

s: Unorganised workers of which age group can register on the e-Shram portal?
x: e-Shram is for unorganised workers aged 16-59 who are not income-tax payers or EPFO/ESIC members.

s: About how many workers from Andhra Pradesh were registered on e-Shram as of July 2026?
x: AP had 88.8 lakh e-Shram registrations (14 July 2026), out of over 31.78 crore nationally.

s: The e-Shram One-Stop Solution (2024) links how many central schemes?
x: The 2024 One-Stop Solution links 15 central schemes, such as PM-SVANidhi, PMSBY and PM-SYM.

s: What is the name of India's first Aadhaar-seeded National Database of Unorganised Workers?
x: The e-Shram portal, launched on 26 August 2021, is India's first Aadhaar-seeded National Database of Unorganised Workers.

s: About how many workers had registered on the e-Shram portal nationally by July 2026?
x: Over 31.78 crore workers were registered on e-Shram, including 88.8 lakh from AP (14 July 2026).

s: Under the Social Security framework, from what age can gig workers register?
x: Gig workers can register from 16, with National and State Social Security Boards; registration does not confer employee status or a minimum wage.

s: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, what is a person who works through online platforms called?
x: A platform worker works through online platforms; a gig worker works outside a traditional employer-employee relationship.

s: Which State enacted the first platform-based gig workers law?
x: Rajasthan's Platform-Based Gig Workers Act, 2023 was the first; Karnataka followed in 2025.

s: What was the NITI estimate of gig workers in India for 2020-21?
x: NITI estimated 77 lakh gig workers; the Economic Survey figure is 120 lakh.

s:
Consider the following statements about gig workers under the Code on Social Security, 2020:
1. Registration gives them employee status.
2. The Code provides for National and State Social Security Boards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Code sets up National and State Social Security Boards, but registration gives no employee status or minimum wage guarantee.

s: Which was the first law in India to recognise gig workers, platform workers and aggregators?
x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 is the first law to recognise aggregators, gig and platform workers.

s: How is the welfare board under Rajasthan's Platform-Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act, 2023 funded?
o: By grants from the Consolidated Fund of India
x: Rajasthan's 2023 Act, the first State gig law, funds its welfare board through a cess on transactions.

s: Which State enacted the Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025?
x: Karnataka enacted this Act in 2025; Rajasthan's 2023 Act was the first.

s: Into which Code has the Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979 been subsumed?
x: The 1979 Act went into the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, not the Social Security Code.

s: What was the displacement allowance under the Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979?
x: The 1979 Act gave a displacement allowance of 50% of monthly wages plus a journey allowance.

s: The OSH Code applies its migrant worker provisions to establishments with at least how many workers?
x: The OSH Code covers establishments with 10 workers, up from 5 under the 1979 Act.

s: Which scheme lets migrant workers draw PDS ration anywhere in India?
x: One Nation One Ration Card lets migrants draw PDS ration anywhere in India.

s: What is the toll-free number of the National Consumer Helpline?
x: The National Consumer Helpline is reached on 1915; it is a helpline with e-commerce convergence partners, not a court.

s: In consumer awareness, what is 'Jagriti'?
x: Jagriti is the Jago Grahak Jago mascot; the online filing portal is e-Jagriti.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: FPO mark – Industrial and consumer products
x: Hallmark certifies gold and silver jewellery. ISI is for industrial and consumer products, Agmark for agricultural produce and FPO for processed fruit products.

s: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been replaced by which of the following laws?
x: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was replaced by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The Legal Metrology Act, 2009 deals with weights and measures; the BIS Act, 2016 governs the ISI mark and hallmarking; the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the 1986 consumer law.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Eco Mark is for eco-friendly products; Hallmark is for gold and silver.

s: In which year was Eco Mark for eco-friendly products introduced?
x: Eco Mark dates from 1991; Agmark is of 1937 and FPO of 1955.

s: In which year was hallmarking of gold made mandatory?
x: Hallmarking of gold became mandatory in June 2021.

s: Which law regulates weights and measures in India?
x: The Legal Metrology Act, 2009 deals with weights and measures.

s: In which year was the Agmark standard for agricultural produce introduced?
x: Agmark for agricultural produce dates from 1937; FPO is 1955 and Eco Mark 1991.

s: In which year was the FPO mark for fruit products introduced?
x: The FPO mark for fruit products dates from 1955; Agmark is from 1937 and Eco Mark from 1991.

s: On which date is National Consumer Day observed in India?
x: National Consumer Day is 24 December; World Consumer Rights Day is 15 March.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the development of the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection?
o: Adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1999, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1985, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2020
Adopted in 1991, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
x: The Guidelines were first adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 to include sustainable consumption and revised in 2015.

s: Whose consumer-rights speech does World Consumer Rights Day commemorate?
x: The day marks John F. Kennedy's 1962 speech on consumer rights.

s: On which date is World Consumer Rights Day observed?
x: World Consumer Rights Day is 15 March; India's National Consumer Day is 24 December.

s: Which State ranked first in consumer justice in the India Justice Report 2026?
x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first in consumer justice in the India Justice Report 2026.

s: Where is the headquarters of Consumers International?
x: Consumers International, founded in 1960, has its head office in London.

s: What was the original name of Consumers International, founded in 1960?
o: International Consumer Protection and Enforcement Network
x: It was founded in 1960 as the International Organisation of Consumers Unions (IOCU) and renamed Consumers International in 1995.

s: Which body can inquire into violations of consumer rights, file class-action complaints and impose penalties?
x: The CCPA can inquire into violations, order recalls and refunds, file class-action complaints and impose penalties.

s: Under Section 21 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, up to what amount may the penalty for a repeat misleading advertisement extend?
x: The penalty may extend to Rs 10 lakh for a first offence and Rs 50 lakh for a repeat offence.

s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, for how long may an endorser of a misleading advertisement be barred for a first offence?
x: An endorser may be barred for up to 1 year, and up to 3 years for a repeat offence.

s: What kind of body is the Central Consumer Protection Authority?
x: The CCPA is an executive agency (from 24 July 2020); the Consumer Commissions are quasi-judicial.

s: Which Act prohibits objectionable advertisements of drugs claiming magic cures?
o: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
x: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 bans objectionable advertisements of drugs.

s: For how long may an endorser of a misleading advertisement be barred for a repeat offence under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
x: An endorser may be barred up to 1 year for a first offence and up to 3 years for a repeat.

s: Which company did the Central Consumer Protection Authority fine Rs 10 lakh over walkie-talkie listings?
x: The CCPA fined Meta Rs 10 lakh over walkie-talkie listings.

s: When did the Central Consumer Protection Authority come into existence?
x: The CCPA came into existence on 24 July 2020; 24 December is National Consumer Day.

s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, within how many days must the admissibility of a complaint be decided, failing which it is deemed admitted?
x: A complaint not decided on within 21 days of filing is deemed to have been admitted.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six consumer rights recognised under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
x: The six rights include safety, information, choice, hearing, redressal and consumer awareness. A right to private ownership is not included in this list.

s: Which one of the following persons would generally be treated as a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
o: A person purchasing services for commercial exploitation
A person purchasing goods solely for a large-scale business activity
A person purchasing goods for resale
A person making an online purchase for personal use
x: The definition includes online and electronic purchases for personal use. A person buying for resale or commercial use is generally excluded.

s: Which of the following bodies was introduced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
x: The 2019 Act introduced the CCPA, along with product liability, e-commerce rules and penalties for adulterated goods; the NCDRC dates from 1988.

s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, up to what claim value is no filing fee charged?
x: Filing is free up to Rs 5 lakh; above that the fee is Rs 200 to Rs 7,500.

s: Which law did the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replace?
x: The 2019 Act replaced the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.

s: If a consumer dies, who may file a consumer complaint in his or her place?
o: The trader who sold the goods
The legal heir of the consumer
x: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the legal heir of a deceased consumer may file a complaint in his or her place.

s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, where can a consumer file a complaint?
o: Only where the seller has its office
Where the complainant lives or works
Only where the goods were bought
x: The 2019 Act lets a consumer file a complaint where he or she lives or works.

s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, to which bodies are consumer mediation cells attached?
x: Mediation cells are attached to the District, State and National Consumer Commissions, not High Courts.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha (1995)?
o: All medical services, including wholly free services, are outside consumer law.
Medical services paid for, including services in hospitals charging some patients, constitute “service” under the Consumer Protection Act.
Medical negligence can never be considered by consumer fora.
Only services provided in government hospitals are covered by consumer law.
x: The 1995 decision held that paid medical services, including services in hospitals that charge some patients, fall within the definition of service under consumer law. Wholly free services are excluded.

s: In which year was Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha decided?
x: In IMA v. V.P. Shantha (1995) the Supreme Court held paid medical services to be a 'service'.

s: Under the 2021 Rules, a consumer complaint involving consideration of ₹40 lakh falls within the original pecuniary jurisdiction of which body?
x: Under the 2021 Rules, the District Commission has jurisdiction over matters up to ₹50 lakh.

s: In which year was the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission set up?
x: The NCDRC was set up in 1988; its original orders are appealable to the Supreme Court within 30 days.

s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, what were the District, State and National Commissions called?
x: They were Consumer Forums under the 1986 Act; they are quasi-judicial bodies, not ordinary civil courts under the CPC.

s: Within how many days does an appeal against an order of a State Consumer Commission lie to the National Commission?
x: State to National is within 30 days; District to State is within 45 days and National to Supreme Court within 30 days.

s: The e-Daakhil facility for online filing has been merged into which portal?
x: The e-Daakhil online filing facility has been merged into the e-Jagriti portal.

s: What is the criterion for determining the pecuniary jurisdiction of a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission?
o: The annual income of the complainant
The compensation claimed by the complainant
The market value of the goods at the time of filing
The value of consideration paid for the goods or services
x: Jurisdiction is determined by the value of consideration paid for the goods or services, not by the compensation claimed.

s: Within how many days does an appeal against an order of a District Consumer Commission lie to the State Commission?
x: District to State appeals lie within 45 days; State to National and National to Supreme Court within 30 days.

s: Under the 2021 Rules, complaints of what value does the State Consumer Commission hear?
x: The 2021 Rules set District up to Rs 50 lakh, State Rs 50 lakh-2 crore, National above Rs 2 crore; the Rs 1-10 crore slab was the original 2019 one.

s: Within how many days does an appeal against an order of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission lie to the Supreme Court?
x: An appeal from the NCDRC lies to the Supreme Court within 30 days.

s: Under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, within what time must the grievance officer of an e-commerce entity acknowledge and redress a consumer complaint, respectively?
x: The Rules require acknowledgement within 48 hours and redressal within one month. 24 hours/15 days, 48 hours/21 days and 72 hours/one month each get at least one period wrong (21 days is the deemed-admission period of Consumer Commissions).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: The prior price shown with a discount must be the lowest price in the preceding 30 days
E-commerce entities must join the National Consumer Helpline convergence process
Search results must not be manipulated
Sponsored listings need not be disclosed if the product is offered at a reduced price
x: Sponsored listings must be clearly disclosed; there is no reduced-price exception.

s: The Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 specified how many dark patterns?
x: The 2023 Guidelines specified 13 dark patterns, including false urgency and basket sneaking.

s: The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 were gazetted on 9 September 2026. From which date did they become effective?
x: The 2026 Amendment Rules were gazetted on 9 September 2026 and are effective from 1 January 2027.

s: Under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, what is an e-commerce entity that owns the goods it sells called?
x: An inventory entity owns the goods it sells, whereas a marketplace entity is only a platform; the Rules treat their liabilities differently.

s: Under the E-Commerce (Amendment) Rules, 2026, the 'prior price' shown must be the lowest price in how many preceding days?
x: The 2026 Rules define prior price as the lowest price in the preceding 30 days.

s: With whom did Nehru draft the Tribal Panchsheel (1952)?
x: Nehru's Tribal Panchsheel was drafted with Verrier Elwin in 1952 and dealt with tribal policy, unlike the international Panchsheel.

s: At the Modi-Xi meeting of September 2025, which principle did China stress as the frame for bilateral ties?
x: China stressed Panchsheel as the framework for India-China ties during the Modi-Xi meeting referred to in the current context.

s: In which year did the UN General Assembly recognise Panchsheel as a principle of international law?
x: The UNGA recognised Panchsheel in 1957, after its absorption into the Bandung Ten Principles (1955) and before Belgrade (1961).

s: With whom did Nehru conclude the Panchsheel Agreement of 1954?
x: Panchsheel was set out in the 29 April 1954 India–China agreement concluded by Nehru and Zhou Enlai.

s: Which one of the following is a principle of Panchsheel (1954)?
x: Peaceful co-existence is one of the five Panchsheel principles. Non-alignment is a separate policy of India, not a Panchsheel principle.

s: On which date did Nehru make the broadcast declaring that India would keep away from power blocs?
x: Nehru's broadcast of 7 September 1946 set out India's stand of keeping away from power blocs, a historical root of its foreign policy.

s: Which of the following pairs related to Panchsheel is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Panchsheel set out in – Preamble of the India–Tibet Region of China trade agreement
x: The Panchsheel agreement was signed on 29 April 1954; 1955 is the year of the Bandung Conference.

s: The Bandung Conference of African and Asian nations was held in April 1955. Which one of the following was adopted at this Conference?
o: The Ten Principles of international peace
x: The Bandung Conference, held in April 1955, adopted the Ten Principles of international peace, which included the principles of Panchsheel.

s: What does non-alignment, as distinguished from neutrality, imply?
o: Avoiding all international issues and conflicts
Supporting whichever bloc is militarily stronger
Active engagement and judging each issue on its merits
x: Non-alignment does not mean passive neutrality; it involves active engagement and an independent assessment of each issue on its merits.

s: To which country did Kwame Nkrumah, a founding leader of the Non-Aligned Movement, belong?
x: Nkrumah was associated with Ghana, Nasser with Egypt, Tito with Yugoslavia and Nehru with India.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The 4th NAM Summit was held at Algiers in 1973. Colombo hosted the 5th Summit in 1976.

s: How many Afro-Asian countries took part in the Bandung Conference of April 1955?
x: The Bandung Conference in Indonesia brought together 29 Afro-Asian countries and adopted the Ten Principles.

s: Where was the first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement held?
x: NAM was founded at the 1st Belgrade Summit in 1961 in Yugoslavia; Bandung 1955 was the Afro-Asian Conference.

s: India hosted which NAM Summit in New Delhi in 1983?
x: The 7th NAM Summit was held in New Delhi in 1983; the 6th was at Havana and the 8th at Harare.

s: Where was the 19th, and latest, NAM Summit held in 2024?
x: The 19th NAM Summit was held at Kampala in 2024; Baku hosted the 18th (2019).

s: Which of the following NAM Summit–venue pairs is correctly matched?
x: The 4th Summit was at Algiers (1973). The 2nd was at Cairo, the 5th at Colombo and the 13th at Kuala Lumpur.

s: Which country was led by Gamal Abdel Nasser, one of the five founders of NAM?
x: Nasser was from Egypt; Nkrumah led Ghana, Sukarno Indonesia and Tito Yugoslavia.

s: Josip Broz Tito, one of the five founders of the Non-Aligned Movement, was the leader of which country?
x: Tito led Yugoslavia, which hosted the first NAM Summit at Belgrade in 1961.

s: Where was the 13th Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement held in 2003?
x: The 13th NAM Summit was held at Kuala Lumpur in 2003; Durban hosted the 12th (1998).

s: Setting up Bhilai with the USSR and Rourkela with West Germany illustrates which determinant of India's foreign policy?
x: Taking aid and technology from both blocs reflects the economy as a determinant; Himalayan frontiers reflect geography.

s: Which one of the following is a core objective of India's foreign policy?
o: Permanent alignment with a single military bloc
x: India's core objectives include independence, security, peace, disarmament and cooperation across ideological lines, not alignment with any military bloc.

s: Which determinant of India's foreign policy is reflected in its Himalayan frontiers and Indian Ocean position?
x: Himalayan frontiers and the Indian Ocean position are the geographic determinants of India's foreign policy.

s: Nehru's idealism and Indira Gandhi's realism illustrate which determinant of India's foreign policy?
x: Leadership styles such as Nehru's idealism and Indira's realism are the political and leadership determinant.

s: How did Jawaharlal Nehru describe India's membership of the Commonwealth?
o: an agreement by free will, to be terminated by free will
a permanent constitutional obligation to the British Crown
a military alliance against the Soviet bloc
a condition imposed by the Indian Independence Act
x: Nehru called Commonwealth membership 'an agreement by free will to be terminated by free will' (UPPSC 2017), consistent with independence from power blocs. It was not a permanent obligation to the Crown, not a military alliance (India followed non-alignment), and not an imposed condition.

s: By which method does Article 51 of the Constitution direct the State to encourage settlement of international disputes?
x: Article 51 directs the State to encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

s: In which entry of the Union List is 'foreign affairs' listed?
x: Entry 10 is foreign affairs; Entry 14 treaties, Entry 15 war and peace, and Entries 11–13 diplomatic representation and the UN.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Executive make treaties?
x: Article 73 covers the Union's executive power, under which the Executive makes treaties; Article 51 is the DPSP on international peace.

s: Which entry of the Union List deals with treaties?
x: Entry 14 covers treaties; Entry 10 is foreign affairs and Entry 15 is war and peace.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Union List Entry 15 – War and peace
x: International peace and settlement of disputes by arbitration is Article 51 (DPSP); Article 73 is the executive power to make treaties.

s: Which phrase sums up India's demand for UNSC reform?
x: India seeks UNSC reform and advocates 'reformed multilateralism', strengthening rather than weakening multilateral bodies.

s: India's G20 Presidency theme of 2023, 'One Earth, One Family, One Future', reflects which principle of India's foreign policy?
x: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam means 'the world is one family', which India's 2023 G20 theme expressed. Panchsheel is the 1954 set of five principles with China; the Gujral Doctrine (1996) concerns non-reciprocal goodwill to smaller neighbours; the Indira Doctrine treats South Asia as India's zone.

s: India opposed the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty of 1968 primarily because it regarded the treaty as
o: a treaty exclusively on chemical weapons
an instrument for ending the United Nations
inconsistent with the principle of peaceful settlement
x: India opposed the NPT because it considered the division between nuclear-weapon states and non-nuclear-weapon states discriminatory.

s: What does Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, a core principle of India's foreign policy, mean?
o: Judging each issue on its merits
x: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam means 'the world is one family', reflected in the G20 2023 theme 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's core foreign-policy principles:
1. India opposes colonialism and apartheid.
2. India supported the NPT (1968) as a fair treaty.
3. The G20 2023 theme 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' reflects Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India opposed the NPT as discriminatory.

s: With whom is strategic autonomy in India's foreign policy associated?
x: Nehruvian idealism, the Indira and Gujral Doctrines belong to individual leaders, while strategic autonomy is associated with all PMs since 1947.

s: What did the Gujral Doctrine, formulated in 1996, emphasise?
o: Non-reciprocal goodwill towards smaller neighbours, non-interference and peaceful settlement
Reciprocal military alliances with larger powers
South Asia as an exclusive military zone
x: The Gujral Doctrine of 1996 emphasised non-reciprocal goodwill towards smaller neighbours, non-interference and peaceful settlement.

s: What did the Indira Doctrine of India's foreign policy stand for?
o: Working with rival powers at the same time
Panchsheel as the basis of ties with China
x: The Indira Doctrine treated South Asia as India's zone; non-reciprocal goodwill is the Gujral Doctrine.

s: Which of the following doctrine–leader pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Gujral Doctrine (1996) was formulated by I.K. Gujral, not Vajpayee.

s: In what capacity do the service chiefs attend the Cabinet Committee on Security?
o: Members in place of the Defence Minister
x: The NSA, Cabinet Secretary and service chiefs attend the CCS as invitees; the Defence Minister is a member.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's National Security Council (NSC):
1. It was set up in 2001.
2. The National Security Adviser is its secretary.
3. Brajesh Mishra was the first National Security Adviser.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the NSC was set up in 1998 (2001 is the ICWA Act). Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the NSA is its secretary and Brajesh Mishra was the first NSA. Hence 2 and 3 only.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA):
1. It was founded in 1943 under Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru.
2. It is based at South Block.
3. The Vice-President of India is its ex officio President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: founded 1943 under Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru. Statement 2 is wrong: it is based at Sapru House, not South Block. Statement 3 is correct: the Vice-President is ex officio President. Hence 1 and 3 only.

s: Which Ministry is scrutinised by Parliament's Standing Committee on External Affairs?
x: The Standing Committee on External Affairs scrutinises the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

s: In which year was the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA) Act passed?
x: The ICWA Act came in 2001; the ICWA itself was founded in 1943 under Tej Bahadur Sapru.

s: When was India's nuclear doctrine adopted by the Cabinet Committee on Security?
x: The CCS adopted the nuclear doctrine on 4 January 2003.

s: In India's Nuclear Command Authority, which is the only body that can authorise the use of nuclear weapons?
x: Only the Political Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, can authorise nuclear use; the Executive Council is chaired by the NSA.

s: Who chairs the Executive Council of India's Nuclear Command Authority?
x: The Executive Council is chaired by the NSA; the Political Council is chaired by the PM.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a tenet of India's nuclear doctrine (2003)?
o: First use against a conventional attack
x: The doctrine rests on credible minimum deterrence, No First Use and retaliation only, so first use is ruled out.

s: Who was the first National Security Adviser of India?
x: Brajesh Mishra was the first NSA; the NSA is the secretary of the National Security Council (1998).

s: Who chairs the Political Council of India's Nuclear Command Authority?
x: The Political Council of the Nuclear Command Authority is chaired by the Prime Minister. It is the only body that can authorise nuclear use.

s: Who is the secretary of India's National Security Council?
x: The National Security Adviser is the secretary of the NSC, set up in 1998.

s: Who is the ex officio President of the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA)?
x: The Vice-President of India is the ex officio President of the ICWA, founded in 1943.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Cabinet Committee on Security?
x: The CCS is the PM with the Ministers of Finance, External Affairs, Home and Defence; Commerce is not a member.

s: Who was reappointed Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs in 2026?
x: In the 2026 reconstitution of the standing committees, Shashi Tharoor was reappointed Chairman of the Committee on External Affairs.

s: Who appoints the Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs?
x: The Committee on External Affairs is serviced by the Lok Sabha, and its Chairman is appointed by the Speaker.

s: Who is the author of 'Half-Lion', a book on P.V. Narasimha Rao?
x: 'Half-Lion: How P.V. Narasimha Rao Transformed India' was written by Vinay Sitapati.

s: Who was the Prime Minister of India when India established full diplomatic relations with Israel in 1992?
x: Building ties with Israel was part of Narasimha Rao's post-Cold War outreach; full relations came in 1992.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rajiv Gandhi — Action plan for nuclear disarmament, 1988
P.V. Narasimha Rao — Ties with Israel
P.V. Narasimha Rao — Lahore bus diplomacy
x: Lahore bus diplomacy is associated with A.B. Vajpayee, not P.V. Narasimha Rao. Rajiv Gandhi is associated with SAARC activism and the 1988 action plan for nuclear disarmament, while P.V. Narasimha Rao pursued ties with Israel.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Tashkent Declaration of 1966 is associated with Lal Bahadur Shastri.

s: With whom is the 'Voice of Global South' initiative associated?
x: Voice of Global South is associated with Narendra Modi; Gujral Doctrine with Gujral, Pokhran-II with Vajpayee and the nuclear deal with Manmohan Singh.

s: With which Prime Minister is the 1988 action plan for nuclear disarmament associated?
x: Rajiv Gandhi presented the 1988 nuclear disarmament action plan, besides the Sri Lanka Accord and SAARC.

s: The Tashkent Declaration of 1966 was signed by which Indian Prime Minister?
x: Lal Bahadur Shastri signed the Tashkent Declaration in 1966; Indira Gandhi is linked with Simla (1972).

s: Under which Prime Minister did India conduct its first nuclear test at Pokhran in 1974?
x: Pokhran-I (18 May 1974), the 'peaceful nuclear explosion', was conducted under Indira Gandhi.

s: In which year did an Indian Prime Minister visit Israel for the first time?
x: Narendra Modi made the first visit to Israel by an Indian Prime Minister in July 2017.

s: The first visit to Israel by an Indian Prime Minister, in July 2017, marked how many years of full diplomatic relations between the two countries?
x: India and Israel set up full diplomatic relations in 1992, so Modi's July 2017 visit marked 25 years.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the first phase of India’s foreign policy, 1946–1962?
x: The 1946–1962 phase is described as optimistic non-alignment, marked by idealism, Panchsheel, NAM, Commonwealth membership and anti-imperialism.

s: Which label is given to the 1991-1998 phase of India's foreign policy?
x: After the USSR's collapse, 1991–98 was the phase of safeguarding strategic autonomy; energetic engagement is the label for 2014 onwards.

s: Which body did India chair in relation to the Korean War?
o: Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war
United Nations Security Council committee on sanctions
South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation council
x: India chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war during the Korean War, with General K.S. Thimayya associated with it.

s: What did the 1962 war with China show the limits of?
x: The 1962 war with China exposed the limitations of the idealist approach associated with the early Nehruvian phase.
