s: Who headed the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war in the Korean War?
x: Gen. K.S. Thimayya headed the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission chaired by India in the Korean War.

s: For how many years was the Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation (9 August 1971) concluded?
x: The treaty was for 20 years and countered the US-China-Pakistan axis during the Bangladesh crisis.

s: The Simla Agreement of 1972 is associated with which principle?
o: Bilateralism and exclusion of a third-party role
Joint control of the Ganga waters by India and Nepal
Internationalisation of the Kashmir issue through the United Nations
x: The Simla Agreement emphasised bilateralism and ruled out a third-party role in resolving India-Pakistan issues.

s: How was Pokhran-I, conducted on 18 May 1974, officially described?
x: India described the 18 May 1974 Pokhran-I test as a peaceful nuclear explosion.

s: Who signed the India-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987, under which the IPKF was deployed, with J.R. Jayewardene?
x: Rajiv Gandhi signed the 1987 Accord with Jayewardene; Indira Gandhi had been assassinated in 1984.

s: On which date did the Pakistan army surrender in Dhaka, completing Bangladesh's liberation?
x: Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971; 9 August 1971 is the Indo-Soviet Treaty.

s: In which year was the Farakka Accord on sharing of Ganga water between India and Bangladesh signed?
x: The Farakka Accord on Ganga water with Bangladesh dates from 1977.

s: In which year did India cede Katchatheevu to Sri Lanka?
x: Katchatheevu was ceded to Sri Lanka in 1974, during the phase of regional assertion.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Lahore Declaration
2. Simla Agreement
3. 123 Agreement
4. Farakka Accord
x: Simla (1972) came before Farakka (1977), the Lahore Declaration (1999) and the 123 Agreement (2008).

s: In which year was the Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation signed?
x: The treaty was signed on 9 August 1971 for 20 years, before the Bangladesh war.

s: Which of the following best explains the foreign-policy significance of LPG reforms?
o: India abandoned all economic engagement with other countries
India replaced economic diplomacy with military diplomacy
India made membership of a Cold War bloc its principal objective
Attracting foreign direct investment and markets became foreign-policy goals
x: Liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation reforms made attracting FDI and accessing markets important foreign-policy goals.

s: Under which Prime Minister was India's Look East Policy launched in 1991-92?
x: Narasimha Rao launched the Look East Policy in 1991–92, bringing India closer to ASEAN.

s: Besides Look East, with which country did India build ties under Narasimha Rao's post-Cold War outreach?
x: In 1991–98, India under Narasimha Rao turned to ASEAN through Look East and opened ties with Israel.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rajiv Gandhi – India-Sri Lanka Accord and IPKF
Jawaharlal Nehru – Look East and economic diplomacy
P.V. Narasimha Rao – Indo-Soviet Treaty and Bangladesh 1971
x: Rajiv Gandhi is associated with the India-Sri Lanka Accord and IPKF. Nehru goes with non-alignment and Panchsheel, Indira Gandhi with the Indo-Soviet Treaty and 1971, and Narasimha Rao with Look East.

s: Which of the following did NOT belong to the 1962–1971 phase of realism and recovery in India's foreign policy?
o: Refusal to sign the NPT in 1968
x: The NSG waiver came in 2008; the other three belong to the 1962–1971 phase.

s: What did India declare itself after Operation Shakti?
o: Signatory to the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state
Permanent member of the UN Security Council
Member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group
x: Following Pokhran-II, India declared itself a nuclear-weapon state. India did not become an NPT-recognised nuclear-weapon state or an NSG member through the tests.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the aftermath of Pokhran-II (1998)?
o: The US imposed sanctions under the Glenn Amendment
No First Use was announced by the Vajpayee government and formalised in 2003
The Jaswant Singh–Strobe Talbott talks preceded the nuclear tests
x: The Singh–Talbott talks followed the tests and sanctions; they did not precede them.

s: In which year was the Hyde Act, a milestone of the Indo-US civil nuclear deal, enacted?
x: The Hyde Act came in 2006, after the 2005 joint statement; the NSG waiver and the 123 Agreement followed in 2008.

s: Which statement about the Kargil War of 1999 is correct?
o: It occurred before both countries conducted nuclear tests and ended through Soviet mediation.
It was settled by the Farakka Accord and involved Bangladesh as a principal party.
It led directly to the signing of the Indo-Soviet Treaty.
It was the first conflict after India and Pakistan had tested nuclear weapons, and US pressure forced Pakistan to withdraw.
x: The Kargil War was the first conflict after both India and Pakistan had tested nuclear weapons; US pressure contributed to Pakistan’s withdrawal.

s: What accompanied the Lahore Declaration of February 1999?
x: The Lahore Declaration came with the Delhi–Lahore bus diplomacy in February 1999.

s: Which government announced India's No First Use policy after Pokhran-II?
x: The Vajpayee government announced No First Use; the formal doctrine followed in 2003.

s: Under which law did the United States impose sanctions on India after Pokhran-II (1998)?
x: The US used the Glenn Amendment for sanctions after 1998; the Hyde Act (2006) and 123 Agreement (2008) belong to the later nuclear deal.

s: With whom did Jaswant Singh hold the India-US dialogue after Pokhran-II?
x: The Jaswant Singh–Strobe Talbott talks followed the sanctions after Pokhran-II.

s: In which year did the Nuclear Suppliers Group grant a waiver to India?
x: The NSG waiver came on 6 September 2008, after the Hyde Act of 2006.

s: When was the India-US 123 Agreement signed?
x: The 123 Agreement was signed in October 2008, a month after the NSG waiver of September 2008.

s: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Pokhran-II nuclear tests were conducted in 1998?
x: Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti, 1998) was conducted under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

s: What was the code name of India's Pokhran-II nuclear tests of 1998?
x: The 1998 Pokhran-II tests were called Operation Shakti, after which India declared itself a nuclear-weapon state.

s: How has India's response to the movement towards a multipolar world since 2008 generally been described?
o: Permanent military alignment with a single superpower
x: India's response to the emerging multipolarity since 2008 is issue-based alignment, under which partnerships vary according to the issue involved.

s: With reference to BRICS, which one of the following is correct?
o: India is an observer but not a founding member.
India is a founding member and chaired BRICS in 2026.
x: India is a founding member of BRICS and chaired the grouping in 2026.

s: During which period did India hold the G20 Presidency?
x: India held the Presidency from December 2022 to November 2023; the African Union became a permanent member and the theme was 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's multi-alignment milestones?
o: India became a full member of the SCO in 2017
Act East was upgraded from Look East in 2014
The Quad comprises India, the US, Japan and Australia
The Neighbourhood First policy dates from 2019
x: Neighbourhood First dates from 2014, not 2019. The other statements are correct.

s: When was the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) signed during the Prime Minister's visit to the United Kingdom?
x: The India-UK CETA was signed during the Prime Minister's UK visit in July 2025.

s: What position did the BRICS New Delhi Declaration, 2026 take on reform of the United Nations?
x: The Declaration backed UN reform, criticised unilateral sanctions and was likened to India's non-aligned past.

s: Which one of the following best illustrates issue-based coalitions?
o: Security cooperation with the United States and energy and defence cooperation with Russia
Withdrawal from both Western and Eurasian institutions
Treating every international issue as a matter of neutrality
A permanent military alliance with one power on every issue
x: Issue-based coalitions are partnerships selected according to the issue, such as security cooperation with the United States and energy and defence cooperation with Russia, rather than fixed alliances.

s: During India's G20 Presidency (2022–23), which body was made a permanent member of the G20?
x: The African Union was made a permanent member of the G20 under India's Presidency.

s: What does multi-alignment refer to?
o: Supporting only developing countries in all disputes
Engaging rival powers at the same time to maximise national interest
Joining a fixed military alliance led by one power
x: Multi-alignment means engaging rival powers simultaneously, such as through the Quad and BRICS/SCO, to maximise national interest.

s: Unlike neutrality, what does strategic autonomy let India do?
o: Stay away from all international disputes
Avoid taking any position on world issues
Judge each issue on its merits without joining military blocs
x: Strategic autonomy means judging each issue on its merits without joining military blocs, so it is active engagement, not neutrality.

s: When was the first Voice of Global South Summit held?
x: India hosted the first Voice of Global South Summit in January 2023, championing developing countries on reformed multilateralism, climate finance and DPI.

s: In which year was the Quad of India, the United States, Japan and Australia, first formed in 2007, revived?
x: The Quad was first formed in 2007 and revived in 2017.

s: When did the Supreme Court uphold the abrogation of Article 370?
x: Article 370 was abrogated on 5 August 2019 and the Supreme Court upheld it in December 2023.

s: On which date was Article 370 abrogated and J&K and Ladakh made Union Territories?
x: Article 370 was abrogated on 5 August 2019; it had become operative on 17 November 1952.

s: Besides bilateral trade, what did Pakistan suspend in response to the abrogation of Article 370?
x: Pakistan downgraded ties and suspended trade and the Samjhauta Express; the Kartarpur Corridor opened later, in November 2019.

s: What did Article 370 of the Indian Constitution, operative from 17 November 1952, provide for?
o: Special status for Jammu and Kashmir
x: Article 370 gave special status to Jammu and Kashmir; it was abrogated on 5 August 2019.

s: On which date did the Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir come into force?
x: The J&K Constituent Assembly approved accession on 17 November 1956 and the State's Constitution came into force on 26 January 1957.

s: After which event was the India-Pakistan Composite Dialogue stopped?
x: The Composite Dialogue (1997, restarted 2004) stopped after 26/11 in 2008.

s: In which year did the attack on the Indian Parliament take place?
x: The Parliament attack was in 2001, followed by Mumbai 26/11 (2008), Uri (2016) and Pulwama (2019).

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Parliament attack of 13 December 2001 was followed by Operation Parakram, involving troop mobilisation. The Balakot airstrike followed Pulwama, while the Composite Dialogue was suspended after Mumbai 26/11.

s: What was India's military response to the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025?
x: After the Pahalgam attack that killed 26 civilians, India launched Operation Sindoor and held the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.

s: What was India's response to the Uri attack of September 2016?
x: Uri led to surgical strikes; Pulwama to Balakot, the Parliament attack to Parakram and Pahalgam to Sindoor.

s: Operation Parakram, a large troop mobilisation, was India's response to which attack?
x: Operation Parakram followed the 13 December 2001 attack on Parliament.

s: What was India's response to the Pulwama attack of 14 February 2019?
x: India answered the Pulwama attack on a CRPF convoy with the Balakot airstrike and withdrew MFN status.

s: Which group carried out the Mumbai 26/11 attacks of November 2008?
x: The Mumbai 26/11 attacks were carried out by Lashkar-e-Taiba; India then suspended the Composite Dialogue.

s: Which terrorist group carried out the Pulwama attack on a CRPF convoy on 14 February 2019?
x: The Pulwama attack was carried out by Jaish-e-Mohammed; India responded with the Balakot airstrike.

s: In which year was the Samjhauta Express between India and Pakistan bombed?
x: The Samjhauta Express (Attari-Lahore) was bombed in 2007.

s: What does the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee deal with?
x: The 1267 committee lists ISIL/Al-Qaida-linked terrorists and entities for asset freezes and travel bans.

s: After which development was Masood Azhar listed by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee in May 2019?
x: Masood Azhar, the chief of Jaish-e-Mohammed, was listed in May 2019 after China lifted its technical hold.

s: During which period did Pakistan remain on the FATF grey list?
x: Pakistan was under increased monitoring on the FATF grey list from June 2018 until its removal in October 2022.

s: In January 1948, India referred the Kashmir issue to the UN Security Council under which Article of the UN Charter?
x: Nehru referred it under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948; UNSC Resolution 47 followed in 1948.

s: On which date did Maharaja Hari Singh sign the Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir?
x: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, after the tribal invasion. Indian troops were airlifted on 27 October.

s: Under the Instrument of Accession signed by Maharaja Hari Singh, which subject stayed with the State?
x: The Instrument (26 October 1947) ceded only defence, external affairs and communications; land revenue stayed with the State.

s: In the 1947 Jammu and Kashmir crisis, which event came immediately after the Instrument of Accession?
o: Airlift of Indian troops to Srinagar
x: The sequence was tribal invasion, accession, airlift of Indian troops to Srinagar and then the First Indo-Pak war; the UN ceasefire came in January 1949.

s: What did UNSC Resolution 47 (1948) on Kashmir call for?
o: A plebiscite conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal
An immediate plebiscite without any withdrawal
Conversion of the ceasefire line into the LoC
x: Resolution 47 called for a plebiscite conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal, which was never held.

s: On which date were Indian troops airlifted to Srinagar after the Instrument of Accession?
x: The accession was signed on 26 October 1947 and troops were airlifted on 27 October.

s: Which of the following was the immediate political outcome of the 1971 India–Pakistan war?
o: The ceasefire line was fixed under the Karachi Agreement.
Bangladesh was created and Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971.
The Indus Waters Treaty was signed.
Pakistan withdrew from Kargil under United States pressure.
x: The 1971 war resulted in the creation of Bangladesh, and Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971.

s: What was India's military response in the 1999 Kargil conflict called?
x: India's response was Operation Vijay; Kargil was the first war between nuclear-armed states, and Pakistan withdrew under US pressure.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1999 Kargil conflict — Operation Grand Slam by India
x: The 1999 Kargil conflict was met by India’s Operation Vijay. Operation Grand Slam was associated with Pakistan’s operations during the 1965 war.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The first Kashmir war was fought in 1947–48, not 1965.

s: In which year was Operation Meghdoot, associated with the Siachen dispute, conducted?
x: India secured the Siachen glacier through Operation Meghdoot in April 1984.

s: Which of the following operation–country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Operation Meghdoot (1984, Siachen) was India's; Gibraltar and Grand Slam were Pakistani operations of 1965.

s: Which document followed the 1965 India-Pakistan war?
x: The 1965 war ended in the Tashkent Declaration (1966); Simla followed the 1971 war.

s: On which date did the UN-arranged ceasefire end the first India-Pakistan war over Kashmir?
x: The 1947-48 war ended with the UN ceasefire of 1 January 1949; the Karachi Agreement of July 1949 then fixed the ceasefire line.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tashkent Declaration (January 1966)?
o: It was mediated by the Soviet Union, with Kosygin playing a key role
It provided for troop withdrawal and return of prisoners of war
It converted the ceasefire line into the Line of Control
x: The ceasefire line became the LoC under the Simla Agreement, 1972, not under Tashkent.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Simla Agreement was between Indira Gandhi and Z.A. Bhutto. Tashkent involved Shastri and Ayub Khan, Lahore involved Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif, and the Indo-Soviet Treaty was India–USSR.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Tashkent Declaration is correct?
o: The strategic Haji Pir Pass was returned to India.
The strategic Haji Pir Pass was returned to Pakistan.
The declaration established the Line of Control.
x: The Tashkent settlement resulted in the return of the strategic Haji Pir Pass to Pakistan.

s: With whom did Atal Bihari Vajpayee hold the Agra Summit of July 2001, which ended without a joint declaration?
x: The Agra Summit was between Vajpayee and Musharraf and ended without a joint declaration.

s: In which year was the Karachi Agreement between India and Pakistan signed?
x: The Karachi Agreement was in 1949, followed by Tashkent (1966), Lahore (1999) and Agra (2001).

s: With whom did Atal Bihari Vajpayee sign the Lahore Declaration of February 1999?
x: Lahore (1999) was Vajpayee–Nawaz Sharif; the Agra Summit (2001) was with Musharraf.

s: Which agreement converted the ceasefire line in Jammu and Kashmir into the Line of Control?
x: The Simla Agreement (1972) turned the ceasefire line into the LoC; Tashkent did not create the LoC.

s: With whom did Indira Gandhi sign the Simla Agreement (2 July 1972)?
x: Indira Gandhi and Z.A. Bhutto signed it; it committed both sides to bilateral settlement and turned the ceasefire line into the LoC.

s: Which country mediated the Tashkent Declaration of January 1966 between India and Pakistan?
x: The Soviet Union mediated the Tashkent Declaration signed by Shastri and Ayub Khan after the 1965 war.

s: Where did Lal Bahadur Shastri die in January 1966, soon after signing a declaration with Ayub Khan?
x: Shastri died at Tashkent just after signing the Tashkent Declaration with Ayub Khan.

s: In which year was the India-Pakistan Composite Dialogue, agreed in 1997, resumed?
x: It resumed in 2004 (Agra 2001 ended without a declaration) and was broken off after 26/11.

s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the eight baskets of the India-Pakistan Composite Dialogue?
o: Peace and security and confidence-building measures
x: The eight baskets included peace and security/CBMs, J&K, Siachen, Wullar Barrage/Tulbul, Sir Creek, terrorism and drugs, economic cooperation, and friendly exchanges. Nuclear disarmament was not listed as a basket.

s: What is Sir Creek?
o: 96-kilometre freshwater river between Punjab and Sindh
96-kilometre tidal estuary between Gujarat and Sindh
154-kilometre mountain pass between Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan
60-kilometre coastal canal between Rajasthan and Sindh
x: Sir Creek is a 96-kilometre tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch between Gujarat and Sindh.

s: On what does Pakistan rely in the Sir Creek boundary dispute?
x: Pakistan cites the 1914 map line, while India relies on the mid-channel thalweg principle.

s: Beyond which point is the line that is at the centre of the Siachen dispute unmarked?
x: The line beyond NJ9842 was left unmarked; India secured the glacier in Operation Meghdoot (1984).

s: Sir Creek, the disputed estuary between Gujarat and Sindh, is about how long?
x: Sir Creek is a 96-km tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch.

s: What did the opening of the Kartarpur Corridor in November 2019 mark?
o: The 550th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak
The centenary of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
The signing of the Lahore Declaration
The 400th anniversary of the birth of Guru Arjan Dev
x: The corridor was opened in November 2019 to commemorate Guru Nanak’s 550th birth anniversary.

s: In which year was the Samjhauta Express between Attari and Lahore started?
x: It began in 1976 after the Simla Agreement and was bombed in 2007.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MFN status between India and Pakistan?
o: India granted MFN status to Pakistan in 1996
India imposed a 100% customs duty on Pakistani goods after withdrawal
Pakistan never reciprocated MFN status to India
India withdrew it in February 2019 after Pulwama
x: The customs duty imposed was 200%, not 100%.

s: Which is the principal land trade route between India and Pakistan?
x: Wagah–Attari is the main land trade route between India and Pakistan.

s: When was the India-Pakistan agreement on the Kartarpur Corridor signed?
x: The agreement was signed in October 2019, giving visa-free access from Dera Baba Nanak to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur.

s: In which district is Dera Baba Nanak, the Indian starting point of the Kartarpur Corridor?
x: The visa-free corridor runs from Dera Baba Nanak (Gurdaspur) to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur (Narowal).

s: What customs duty did India impose on Pakistani goods on withdrawing MFN status in February 2019?
x: After Pulwama, India withdrew MFN (granted in 1996) and imposed 200% customs duty.

s: In which district of Pakistan is Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur, located?
x: The Kartarpur Corridor links Dera Baba Nanak (Gurdaspur) with Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur, in Narowal district.

s: For how many years was the India-Pakistan agreement on the Kartarpur Corridor renewed in October 2024?
x: The Kartarpur Corridor agreement was renewed for 5 years in October 2024.

s: Who signed the Indus Waters Treaty (Karachi, 1960), brokered by the World Bank, with Ayub Khan?
x: Nehru and Ayub Khan signed the Treaty; Shastri and Ayub Khan were the Tashkent pair.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the Permanent Indus Commission?
o: It has three Commissioners from India and one from Pakistan.
It is a court composed of judges from the Hague.
It consists only of representatives appointed by the World Bank.
It consists of one Commissioner from each country.
x: The Permanent Indus Commission has one Commissioner from India and one from Pakistan.

s: From which date did the Cabinet Committee on Security place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance?
x: Following the Pahalgam attack on 22 April 2025, the treaty was placed in abeyance from 23 April 2025.

s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which western rivers were allocated to Pakistan?
x: The western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab go to Pakistan, though India keeps limited rights such as run-of-river hydropower.

s: Under Article IX of the Indus Waters Treaty, to whom are 'differences' referred?
x: Questions go to the Permanent Indus Commission, differences to a Neutral Expert and disputes to a Court of Arbitration.

s: What was the stated condition for ending the abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty?
o: Withdraw from the Permanent Indus Commission
Credibly and irrevocably give up support for cross-border terrorism
Return all western rivers to India
Accept the jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice
x: The abeyance was to continue until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably gives up support for cross-border terrorism.

s: The Indus Waters Treaty gives India about what share of the waters?
x: India gets about 20% of the waters, and the Treaty is criticised for lacking aquifer and drought clauses.

s: On what ground did India reject the 2026 ruling of the PCA Court of Arbitration in the Ratle case?
o: Was appointed by the United Nations
x: The Court held the treaty remains in force and issued interim measures; India rejected it, asserting the court had no jurisdiction.

s: On which date was the Indus Waters Treaty signed at Karachi?
x: Nehru and Ayub Khan signed the Treaty at Karachi on 19 September 1960, brokered by the World Bank.

s: What is India's stand on the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling on the Indus Waters Treaty?
x: India has rejected, not accepted, the PCA ruling, while keeping the Treaty in abeyance and seeking renegotiation.

s: Who appointed both a Neutral Expert and a Court of Arbitration over the Kishanganga and Ratle projects under the Indus Waters Treaty?
x: The World Bank, broker of the 1960 Treaty, appointed both because the Treaty sets no order between them.

s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allocated to India?
x: The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej went to India; the western rivers to Pakistan.

s: On which river are India's Kirthai-II and Sawalkote hydropower projects planned?
x: After the Treaty was put in abeyance, India moved Kirthai-II (930 MW) and Sawalkote (1,856 MW) on the Chenab.

s: Under Article IX of the Indus Waters Treaty, to which body are 'disputes' referred?
x: Questions go to the Permanent Indus Commission, differences to a Neutral Expert and disputes to a Court of Arbitration.
